title: Stitch SDK handover templates & slim playflow (draft)
content:
TL;DR: Lightweight handoff + 15-minute first-run checklist for the new Stitch SDK. Aim: let a solutions-engineer or small customer team run a working demo (curl + minimal JS) and collect telemetry that surfaces regressions quickly. Not a full PRD — a compact companion for SE handoffs and docs authors.

Audience:
- Solutions engineering doing customer demos
- Docs writer producing the quickstart
- Oncall / field eng who need smoke tests or repro steps

Goals:
- Cut onboarding time to first successful request to ~15 minutes (including env setup).
- Provide one canonical curl and one tiny JS snippet for quick verification.
- Telemetry keys + cheap smoke checks to detect common failure modes (auth, model mismatch, latency spike).
- Reusable Slack/email templates for handoff to SE / Customer Success.

What this is NOT:
- Not the full SDK reference. It's intentionally narrow: boot a client, send a prompt, verify results, collect minimal telemetry.

Quick flow (15-min happy path):
1) Clone the example repo (or use local snippet) — link in linked_artifacts.
2) Export creds (env var names below).
3) Run curl smoke request -> expect 200 + safety check string.
4) Run node quicktest.js -> expect streaming token output within 3s.
5) Open telemetry dashboard (DevExp / Stitch quickdash) -> check token count, p50 latency, error rate.
6) If any step fails, run local logs command (stitchctl logs --last 50) and paste to Slack template.

Environment (minimal):
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (user-scoped key for demo account)
- STITCH_MODEL (e.g., redwood/stitch-1.0)
- REGION (optional, default us-west-2)
- NODE_ENV=development for local examples

15-minute checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Get API key from onboarding email (or create demo key in Console)
- [ ] Set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var locally
- [ ] Run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"stitch-1.0","prompt":"Write a two-line haiku about debugging"}'
  - expected: HTTP 200, body contains 2-3 short lines, no safety-block
- [ ] Run: node quicktest.js (script below)
  - expected: stream begins within 2s, total tokens < 150 for this prompt
- [ ] Open Quickdash: check p50 < 300ms per-token, tokens_consumed metric spikes by ~50
- [ ] If error, copy logs & create Jira ticket DE-#### with attached logs

Minimal curl example (canonical):
- curl command as above (keeps simple payload). Use model: "stitch-1.0" in examples.

Minimal JS snippet (quicktest.js):
- const http = require('https');
- // pseudo-example, intentionally small for copy/paste into an SE sandbox
- const opts = {
    hostname: 'api.redwood.ai',
    path: '/v1/generate',
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
  };
- const req = http.request(opts, res => { res.on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d)); });
- req.write(JSON.stringify({ model: process.env.STITCH_MODEL || 'stitch-1.0', prompt: 'Summarize this repo in one sentence.' }));
- req.end();

Telemetry & smoke signals (what to watch):
- key metrics (Quickdash names): tokens_consumed, request_5xx_rate, p50_token_ms, cold_start_rate
- sanity assertions: tokens_consumed > 0 on success; p50_token_ms < 400ms for hosted tier; 5xx rate = 0 for test window
- logs: look for "KV cache miss" spikes (indicates model mismatch/prefix caching not primed)

Rollout gating (for a new SDK release):
- prerequisite: CI passing + e2e quicktest green on main branch
- canary: enable kits for 5 internal accounts -> monitor tokens and 5xx for 24h
- guardrails: auto rollback if 5xx > 0.5% or p50 increases by >100ms

Handoff templates (copy/paste):
- Slack (to #sdk-boarding):
  "Heads-up: Handing off Stitch SDK demo to @Customer{acct}. Quick steps: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run curl sample, run node quicktest.js. If you hit auth issues, check DE-4321. Docs: <confluence link>. @SE-team please confirm run-by."
- Email (to CS + SE + customer):
  Subject: Stitch SDK quick demo + access
  Body:
  Hi {Name},

  Attached are two minimal ways to run the Stitch SDK demo: a single curl and a tiny Node script. You should be able to verify in ~15 minutes.
  Steps: 1) set REDWOOD_API_KEY 2) run curl 3) run quicktest.js 

  If anything fails, paste logs to the Jira ticket DE-4321 or ping #sdk-boarding. 
  Thanks, Jordan (on behalf of DevExp)

Common failure modes & quick remediations:
- auth 401: ensure key has the demo-scope flag or use a personal test key
- model mismatch / 404: check STITCH_MODEL vs Console model alias; update env var
- slow stream: try REGION=us-west-2 or switch to a smaller batch-size profile (see DE-4387)
- safety-block / filter triggers: shrink prompt, remove PII; file a regression if unexpected

Open questions (TODOs):
- Which demo key should be long-lived vs ephemeral? (Lina to confirm with security)
- Where should we host the one-click run in Playground? (must not expose production keys)
- Should quicktest.js be an official packaged snippet in the SDK repo or in a separate examples repo? (tradeoffs: discoverability vs noise)

Next steps (short):
- Lina: confirm demo-key policy (DE-4321) — due 2024-11-01
- Evan: add quickdash link to README and wire token metric in the example (PR #58)
- Priya: author a 5-min video walkthrough (script draft attached in linked artifacts)
- Jordan: consolidate into final quickstart doc once demo-key policy is decided

Appendix: sample env var table (for copy into SE message)
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_demo_xxx
- export STITCH_MODEL=stitch-1.0
- export REGION=us-west-2

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep examples minimal; avoid advanced flags that confuse new users.
- Consider a 1-click “playground run” that sets a transient key and runs quicktest behind the scenes (security review required).
- Keep a small set of canonical prompts to avoid safety noise in demos.

If you use this doc to run a demo, please paste results into the ticket DE-4321 (template at the top of the ticket) so we can iterate on failures.

-- end --
